title: Haymaker: Fighting Game Sound Effects
shortText: 134 fighting game SFX: hits on 7 strengths, hit stops, guard, parry, throws, super, combo counter, KO. WAV + OGG.
html:
Every system cue a fighting game fires

134 fighting game sound effects in one arcade voice: hits on 7 strengths to the body and the face, a hit stop for every strength, guard and guard break, parry, throws, the super, an energy projectile, a 10 step combo counter, the round and the KO.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 23 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The whole body strength ladder from the jab to the critical, three hit stops, a guard and a parry, the whole super (charge loop, flash, activation, finisher), the combo counter at steps 1, 5 and 10, the round bell, the KO, a select cursor and the dojo loop.

Hits graded like a fighting game grades them

The recorded punch libraries we read give you a pile of punches. A fighting game needs the GRADE: a jab and a heavy graded apart, a counter hit that stands apart from both, a critical bigger than all of them. So every strike here exists at 7 strengths (jab, light, medium, heavy, launcher, counter, critical) on 2 targets (the body, darker, and the face, brighter), and each strength has its own hit stop: a short crack and crunch to play on the first frame of the freeze, so the freeze itself is heard.

Wiring it is one string: "hit_" + target + "_" + strength. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: every rung is longer than the one before it, the strength changes the sound and so does the target (49 grid pairs, 0 alike).

The whole system, not just the hits

  • 14 guard and defence sounds: a guard at three strengths, chip damage, guard crush, guard break, a parry, a just defend, a perfect block, an armour absorb and a pushblock.
  • 11 throw and floor sounds: a grab, a whiffed grab, the slam, a throw tech, wall bounce, wall splat, ground bounce, two knockdowns, a tech roll and a wake up.
  • 9 super and meter sounds: the meter filling one, two and three bars, meter full, a charge loop, the super flash, the activation, the finisher impact and a burst escape.
  • 6 energy projectile sounds: charge, release, a travel loop, impact, two projectiles clashing and a reflect.
  • 14 combo sounds: a 10 step combo counter that gets brighter every step, a combo drop, a combo finisher, a first attack and a reversal.
  • 13 round sounds: the round bell at the start and the end, a fight start slam, timer ticks, time up, the KO, a slow motion KO, a double KO, a perfect, a draw and a round win.
  • 13 select and versus screen sounds: cursors, lock in, cancel, a random select spin, stage select, the versus panels and the versus slam, pause and menu cues.
  • 13 movement sounds: dash, back dash, jumps, a double jump, landings, air recovery, a footwork shuffle and a crouch.
  • 3 stun sounds and 5 arena loops: a stun hit, a dizzy stars loop and the recovery; a dojo, a street at night, a rooftop, an arcade and a training room.
  • 33 strike sounds in all: the grid, the hit stops, swings at four strengths, kicks, whiffs and a flurry barrage.

Four of these are whole lifecycles (the super, the projectile, the dizzy stun and the throw), and the 18 pairs of stages inside them all measure as different sounds, never one cue renamed.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group, role and strength.
  • 7 ladders a game can index by number, all measured to climb: 34 steps, 0 failing.
  • 8 seamless loops of 2.0 to 6.0 seconds with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 12 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness, so the tenth kick is not the first one again.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.06 dB, so a critical hit and a menu cursor share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1225 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our battle packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in Akatsuki, Jianghu, Sengoku and Steel and Bone (66330 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 66330 of 66330 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json. The studio shares a craft; the packs do not share files.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised arcade sounds designed for games, not recordings of real punches: a game that wants recorded realism wants a recorded library. No voice and no announcer in this pack, and nothing musical: the round bell is one struck bell, the KO and the super are designed impacts and sweeps, never a jingle. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover illustration is AI generated, and the store graphics are made by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Arena Call 01, the announcer this pack leaves out: round, fight, KO, time, draw and perfect calls as spoken lines.
  • Bout, a one on one fighting game scene for RPG Maker MZ.
  • Akatsuki, our anime and JRPG battle suite.
  • Jianghu, wuxia and xianxia sound effects.
  • Sengoku, shinobi and samurai sound effects.
